note: Independently rejudged against RFC 4271 Sections 8, 8.2.1, 8.2.1.2 and 6.7, the relevant RFC 4486 Section 4 refusal distinction, RFC 6286 collision updates, RFC 6608 unexpected-message handling, RFC 7606 UPDATE handling and the RFC Editor inline-errata rendition. Section 8 states: "The data structures and FSM described in this document are conceptual and do not have to be implemented precisely as described here, as long as the implementations support the described functionality and they exhibit the same externally visible behavior." Section 8.2.1's incoming requirement therefore binds connection behavior, not the presence of a particular Session/FSM object. The positive listener unit receives Ze's OPEN on the admitted incoming TCP connection before sending its remote OPEN and completes that connection's OPEN/KEEPALIVE exchange while the outgoing connection has received no remote OPEN. The separate negative reaches EOF on a held incoming connection, observes exactly one retry increment and released pending ownership, then establishes the original held connection on its original TCP socket. These are useful success and failure-isolation outcomes, not object-count assertions alone. Both current native records replace newIncomingSession's isolated exchange with the incumbent: main observed each clean named unit PASS and each broken named unit FAIL, respectively missing incoming OPEN and missing the candidate's held DelayOpen state. The input isolates this per-connection ownership obligation and the two polarities are separate functions. Reachable producers preserve the incoming Session, reader and timer lifecycle through collision selection; local capacity refusal before that exchange is permitted by Section 6.7 and RFC 4486 Section 4 and does not owe an otherwise unused FSM object. Current capacity refusal sends 6/5; an actual OPEN-based collision loser retains 6/7. Additional untagged capacity controls observed by main exercise refusal/EOF, the same admitted connection's true collision outcome and useful incumbent traffic. They support the refusal interpretation without becoming extra tagged whole-row proof. This judgment covers the stated incoming handshake and failure ownership obligation; it does not claim every plugin callback, every BGP requirement or live interoperability has been proven. A separately identified provisional role-callback publication defect remains owned by its correction and independent closure work.
upgrade_reason: The earlier partial finding inferred a universal conformance gap solely because refused additional TCP sockets did not construct Session/FSM objects. That inference contradicted RFC 4271 Section 8's explicit conceptual-structure provision and ignored Section 6.7 and RFC 4486 Section 4's permitted local refusal behavior. Re-read the primary text, actual admission/handshake/retirement producers, both complete tagged bodies and renewed native records. The existing bodies already discriminate the required per-connection handshake and isolated failure behavior; correcting their claim wording and withdrawing the structural-only gap warrants enforced rather than constructing unused objects or requiring unlimited incoming admission. All existing assertions remain intact.
